apps.subtitle: PlayStation 2 emulator for ARM64
apps.localizedDescription: A free and open-source PlayStation 2 (PS2) emulator based on PCSX2, with native ARM64 JIT recompilers. Play PS2 games on your phone, PC, or gaming handheld.

versions.localizedDescription:
Automated nightly build for community testing (unsigned).

Every download is named `ARMSX2-nightly-DATE-COMMIT-PLATFORM`, so builds
from different nights stay distinguishable after you have downloaded them.

- macOS arm64: macOS-arm64.tar.xz
- Linux arm64: Linux-arm64-4K-pages.AppImage on most distros, or the 16K one on Asahi Linux and other Apple Silicon kernels (run getconf PAGESIZE if unsure)
- Windows arm64: Windows-arm64.zip
- RetroArch on Linux arm64: Linux-arm64-libretro-core.tar.zst, a 4K-page build
- Bare-display kmsdrm handhelds: Linux-arm64-SDL-handheld.tar.zst, a 4K-page build (Rocknix and Batocera run compositors, so use the Qt AppImage there instead)
- Android: Android-arm64.apk (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)
- iOS: iOS-arm64.ipa, unsigned, sideload it (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)

Coming from an old nightly? Nightlies are now a separate app, ARMSX2 Nightly, next to stable.

- Android: stable cannot install over an old nightly. Back up your saves and memory cards, uninstall the old nightly, then install the stable APK.
- iOS: your old nightly is the ARMSX2 iOS app and still has your saves. Copy them into ARMSX2 Nightly with the Files app.

## What's new
- Tests: three Linux-only expectations are skipped on macOS
- VU program cache: a copy the preload held is not answered after the session wrote the file
- tests: VuAotCache.UnusableSavedCodeFallsBackToThePlan no longer races the cache's preload thread
- vu-aot: the clear with no VM running follows the global setting, not the config a game ended with
- vu-aot: the compile worker takes the process's processor mask, not that of the thread that starts it
- Big Picture: a switch for the VU1 ahead-of-time compiler in the System settings
- Qt: a checkbox for the VU1 ahead-of-time compiler in the Advanced settings
- vu-aot: turning EnableVUAot off with no VM running clears the compiled cache too
- VU program cache: opened by the first reset, not by mVUinit
- Android: a switch for the VU1 ahead-of-time compiler, in the in-game Performance menu and the Performance settings
- vu-aot: turning EnableVUAot off clears the compiled cache
- vu-aot: EnableVUAot defaults to on
- Discord: remote play shows as "Playing remote play (2 of 2)" with the game
- core_test: the item-stamp test reads the IOP's clock at the moment of the apply, not its published position
- IOP thread: the sleep-handshake hammer runs until it has covered enough sleeps, not for a fixed number of rounds
- IOP thread: an idle IOP watches the watermark for 500 us before it sleeps, not 50
- eerunner: --iop-idle-spin-us, the Threaded IOP thread's idle-watch window
- IOP thread: no acquire loads in the event test after the watermark's release store
- IOP thread: the OSD's IOP line is drawn on every frame, not only on the frames that refresh it
- Thread pinning: order the processors by the kernel's capacity table, so a handheld pins to its big cores
- IOP thread: Android settings for the IOP thread and its lag bound
- IOP thread: SharedWord uses the compiler's atomic builtins, since Android NDK 28 has no std::atomic_ref
- IOP thread: Qt and Big Picture settings for the IOP thread and its lag bound
- IOP thread: its CPU time is shown with the EE, GS and VU1 threads' on the OSD
- IOP thread: a concurrent IOP thread takes a processor of its own in the thread placement
- IOP thread: the lag check trusts the last IOP position it saw while that is within the bound
- IOP thread: the EE's and the IOP's private words and counters sit on separate cache lines
- IOP thread: an idle IOP watches the watermark, and only a sleeping one is woken
- IopThread/EeBridge.h: the header comment says where the slice break reads the mode
- IOP thread: the hold test also covers a lifecycle hold, which falls back to sleeping while it waits
- IOP thread: a hold no longer gives up when the VM is stopping
- IOP thread: the lag-bound object test no longer depends on which thread gets there first
- IOP thread: a test that stopping a thread started inside an event test drops its start hold
- IOP thread: a Threaded thread started inside an EE event test stays stopped until the next one
- IOP thread: Threaded tests for what a mutation run showed they missed
- eerunner and the OSD report the Threaded IOP counters, and eerunner can stress the IOP thread's lifecycle
- IOP thread: in Threaded mode the host thread's analog button toggle is posted to the IOP thread
- IOP thread: Threaded runs: the IOP paces itself from the EE's watermark, and the SIF pumps run on the EE thread (variant R)
- IOP thread: the thread object counts the EE's waits, says when the IOP is stopped, and takes a hook at each hold
- arm64: the register allocator's state is per thread, so an EE block and an IOP block can compile at once
- IOP thread: a VM that Initialize leaves Paused holds the IOP, like one that SetState pauses
- eerunner: work a hotkey defers to the CPU thread runs under the same released pause hold
- eerunner: --host-action runs its hotkeys without the frame-by-frame pause hold
- core_test: the DualShock 2 record includes the stick dead zone
- core_test: the guitar's whammy bar is saved in a state and restored from it
- core_test: the IOP thread's FPCR after a CPU settings change
- IOP thread: the CPU thread holds the IOP around the volume, mute, speed and memory card swap hotkeys, and the audio, DEV9, USB and memory card entries assert it
- IOP thread: pad and USB vibration are posted to the CPU thread in Threaded mode, and a blocking Host::RunOnCPUThread from the IOP thread asserts
- IOP thread: the physical-disc thread's new-disc callback goes to the IOP thread through a gated host command queue
- IOP thread: the pad input fields are relaxed atomics, with a record of what every pad type answers to a poll
- IOP thread: Devel ownership asserts, and the hold the ELF entry point hook was missing
- IOP thread: the EE's entries into IOP state take a hold, and a PS1 mode switch turns Lockstep off
- IOP thread: in Lockstep the EE's blanking, its IRQ to the IOP and its once-a-frame jobs go through the E2I queue
- IOP thread: the IOP position is the EE's 64-bit cycle less what the IOP is owed, with a test across 2^32
- R5900.h: the plain _cpuEventTest_Shared() is an inline wrapper, so no second copy of the event test is built
- core_test: the plain _cpuEventTest_Shared() does what the Off instance does
- x86 files back to master: _cpuEventTest_Shared() stays as a plain function that forwards to the Off instance
- IOP thread: ChooseModeFor takes the host and conditions, so the demotion of Threaded can be tested
- eerunner: --settings-churn applies a settings change mid-run, and a run reports what the IOP thread did
- core_test: the Lockstep event test, its handoff, the holds and the thread's FPCR
- IOP thread: Lockstep runs the IOP's slice of every EE event test on the IOP thread
- IOP thread: the test-harness condition is a run-time flag, not a compile-time define
- IOP thread: Lockstep and Threaded both resolve to Off on a host that is not ARM64
- Build files: pcsx2/IopThread/SharedWord.h is listed in CMake and in the Visual Studio project
- The other words the EE and IOP threads share are relaxed atomics: ICFG, the GS video mode, the memory card busy frame
- SBUS: the registers are read and written with atomic operations on both sides
- core_test: what each side does to the SBUS registers, value by value, before they are made atomic
- SIF1: the pump's loop body is two functions, Sif1EeStep and Sif1IopStep
- SIF0: the pump's loop body is two functions, Sif0IopStep and Sif0EeStep
- core_test: scripted SIF0 and SIF1 transfers pin what the two pumps do, recorded before they are split
- IOP JIT: remove iopDispatcherEvent, a stub nothing ever jumps to
- EeBridge: the places where IOP-side code reaches into EE scheduling or state go through one inline function each
- IopBridge: the places where the EE reaches into IOP state go through one inline function each
- Patch: the vsync patches for IOP memory are applied in a pass of their own
- R5900: the IOP slice and the next-event scheduling in the event test become two named functions
- IOP thread: the thread object, its pacing loop, holds and Lockstep handoff, not yet used
- IOP thread: the queues and flags the EE and IOP threads talk through, not yet used
- IOP thread: Lockstep resolves on any host, whatever the core count or core type
- IOP thread: settings keys, GameDB key and IopThread::ResolveMode, with no behaviour
- core_test: FingerprintIop reads without changing anything, and each hash follows its own state
- eerunner twin: record the IOP-side state (SPU2, SIF, SIO, cdvd) in every frame
- mVU progcache: the program file times go through UTF-8 paths
- vu-aot: an installed program joins the list of every start PC it holds a block for
- mVU progcache: preload the most recently used programs first, and delete the ones unused for 60 days
- mVU persist: a payload recorded by another build is refused, and replaced by the next save
- vu-aot: the install audit and install tests cover a region that keeps a w lane in memory
- vu-aot: the dead-value sweep and the w-lane scan cost less to compile
- vu-aot: a home whose w lane a loop never writes keeps it in memory
- vu-aot: roots the builder declined are saved, and not asked for again
- vu-aot: a value with no use left gives its register back
- pcsx2-eerunner: --vuaot-no-install uses loaded vu-aot sidecars as plans only
- vu-aot: saved region code is installed as a program loads
- vu-aot: VI arithmetic writes straight into its operand's home
- vu-aot: a VI in a region's register home keeps its upper bits
- VU interpreter: the end of a program no longer waits for an FMAC or an ILW in flight
- vu-aot: node registration, branch patching and the first-region count as helpers
- vu-aot: the worker describes every address in a region's code
- vu-aot: a region's conditional link tests the VI in one compare
- vu-aot: sidecar format 2, whose records can carry their region code
- VU tests: console rows for what the end of a program waits for

Full changelog: https://github.com/ARMSX2/ARMSX2/compare/nightly-20261016...0d525e4bdb02c1111dc47e313ee460481c11874d
